## Verified core hazards

An energy vortex is a speed-20, level-6 monster with two distinct engulfing attacks (shock and energy drain) plus a separate passive electric attack. Its passive is defined as `AT_NONE AD_ELEC 0d4`; in NetHack 5.0, the passive-damage code rolls `m_lev + 1` dice when `damn` is zero, so a level-6 energy vortex’s base passive roll is 7d4, not 0 damage. The electric passive has a separate 2-in-3 trigger while the vortex is alive, uncancelled, and adjacent. 【turn716019view2】【turn407449view0】【turn347056view2】

A fire vortex is speed 22 and has a passive `0d4` fire attack; a fire elemental is speed 12 and also has a passive `0d4` fire attack. Their active attacks are separate from those passive effects. 【turn716019view1】【turn131033view0】

Written Elbereth is not a universal answer: in 5.0 it does not work on the Elemental Planes, and a vortex cannot be engraved against while it has swallowed the hero. The 5.0 `onscary()` check does not list energy vortices or fire vortices among the monster-type exceptions to written Elbereth, so on an ordinary level they are not intrinsically immune to it. 【turn193943view0】【turn937700view4】

# R01 Energy vortex and other fast passive monsters (A)

## Summary

- Do not melee an energy vortex or fire vortex without a compelling reason. The passive is much larger than the `0d4` notation suggests: at base monster level, the energy vortex rolls 7d4 shock and the fire vortex rolls 9d4 fire when its passive triggers. The roll scales with the monster's actual level. [5.0 `monsters.h`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/include/monsters.h?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1076-L1085) [5.0 `uhitm.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/uhitm.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L5552-L5803)
- Throwing is safer than melee, but a few ordinary daggers are not a dependable kill plan. A +0 dagger does only 1d3 against these huge monsters; at base monster levels the rough expected successful-hit counts are about 14 for an energy vortex and 18 for a fire vortex or fire elemental. These are estimates, not guaranteed kill counts. [5.0 `objects.h`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/include/objects.h?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L184-L186) [5.0 `weapon.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/weapon.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L197-L282) [5.0 `makemon.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/makemon.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L967-L1010)
- Treat an unidentified `v` map glyph as dangerous. It identifies the vortex monster class, not the specific vortex species. Some other vortexes are also fast, even though they do not have a damaging passive. [5.0 `defsym.h`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/include/defsym.h?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1702-L1797)
- Written Elbereth can scare energy and fire vortices on eligible levels, but not in Gehennom or the Endgame. A fire vortex is therefore a particularly bad monster to rely on Elbereth against in its usual Gehennom setting. [5.0 `monmove.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/monmove.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L222-L280) [5.0 `monsters.h`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/include/monsters.h?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1096-L1100)
- If swallowed, use an escape effect rather than trying to engrave or relying on an ordinary retreat. A wand of opening self-zapped, or a successful slow-monster effect on the engulfer, can release the hero. Self-teleportation is another option when teleportation is allowed. [5.0 `zap.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/zap.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L202-L215) [5.0 `zap.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/zap.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2566-L2787) [5.0 `teleport.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/teleport.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L453-L466)

Fast passive-hazard species by the >12 criterion: energy vortex, fire vortex, and rust monster. Fire elemental is exactly speed 12, so it is not in that group. The other listed hazardous passives are not faster than the speed-12 comparison point.

Additional passive-definition exception: green slime has an `AT_NONE AD_SLIM` entry in its monster definition, but the 5.0 `passive()` handling does not implement it as a passive slime attack. Its dangerous sliming contact is an active attack, not a damaging passive. Do not classify it as a working passive counterattack. ## Bot rules

The rules below assume the standard NetHack command interface. Replace inventory letters with the letters actually read from the current inventory; never hard-code them. Direction keys below use the conventional vi layout (`h j k l y u b n`). UNVERIFIED for a particular NLE wrapper: confirm that its configured keymap is vi-style before using those direction characters.

### Rule 1 — Treat an unidentified vortex as dangerous

- Trigger = Map contains `v`, and the latest visible message or observation does not identify the species.
- Action = Do not move toward it. If there is a clear retreat route, move away using the direction key opposite its position (`h/j/k/l/y/u/b/n` in vi keymap). If it is still at range and a clear shot exists, use Rule 2.
- Done when = The vortex is no longer an immediate threat: it has been killed, is no longer pursuing, or the hero has reached a position where it cannot immediately engulf or attack.
- If it fails = If it closes to adjacent range, do not spend turns trying to identify its subtype. Use an available escape item or retreat route; if swallowed, use Rules 5–7.
- Evidence = `v` represents the vortex class rather than an individual species (`include/defsym.h`, 5.0.0); energy and fire vortex definitions include engulf and passive attacks (`include/monsters.h`, 5.0.0).

### Rule 2 — Prefer thrown daggers to a sword attack

- Trigger = A hostile monster is identified as an energy vortex, fire vortex, or fire elemental; or the bot sees an unidentified `v` glyph and chooses the conservative vortex policy. The target is visible at range and the hero has a dagger in inventory.
- Action =
  1. Press `t` (throw).
  2. At the object-selection prompt, enter the inventory letter for a dagger.
  3. If a quantity prompt appears, enter `1` and confirm.
  4. Enter the direction key pointing at the monster.
  5. Re-read the map and messages before throwing again.
- Done when = A kill message is received, or the target is no longer present and the bot has independently established that it is dead or no longer a threat. Mere disappearance from view is not proof of a kill.
- If it fails = If the target moves adjacent, stop treating dagger attrition as a viable plan. Use a teleport/escape item or retreat. Do not switch automatically to the long sword.
- Evidence = `dothrow.c` handles projectile attacks; `uhitm.c` calls the passive routine in the melee path. Dagger large-target damage is `1d3` (`objects.h`, `weapon.c`), while monster HP is randomized and level-adjusted (`makemon.c`). All references: NetHack 5.0.0.

Dagger estimate for the bot: use about 14 successful hits against a base-level energy vortex and about 18 against a base-level fire vortex/fire elemental as rough averages for +0 daggers. Do not set these as kill thresholds. Actual monster level, HP roll, dagger enchantment, hit rate, and any damage bonuses change the result. A few daggers are not a reliable full-HP kill plan.

### Rule 3 — Use Elbereth only where it is known to work

- Trigger = A hostile monster is approaching on a level where written Elbereth is enabled; the hero is not swallowed and can reach the floor.
- Action =
  1. Press `E` (engrave).
  2. At the engraving-method prompt, enter `-` for engraving with fingers.
  3. At the text prompt, type `Elbereth`.
  4. Confirm the text entry.
  5. Keep the hero on or behind the engraved tile as appropriate to the movement plan.
- Done when = The engraving is visible on the map and the monster is respecting the scare effect.
- If it fails = Do not repeat the engraving blindly. If the level is Gehennom or the Endgame, assume written Elbereth will not repel the monster. Use another escape method.
- Evidence = `engrave.c` implements the engraving commands and prevents engraving while swallowed; `monmove.c` implements `onscary()` and the level restrictions (NetHack 5.0.0).

### Rule 4 — Teleport away before engulfment when necessary

- Trigger = A dangerous vortex is closing in, the hero has a known wand of teleportation or a teleportation scroll, and ordinary movement is no longer a reliable way to maintain distance.
- Action =
  - Wand: press `z`, select the known wand of teleportation, then enter `.` to zap yourself.
  - Scroll: press `r`, select the known scroll of teleportation, and answer any read/confirmation prompt as required.
- Done when = The hero has relocated and is no longer swallowed or adjacent to the threat.
- If it fails = If teleportation is blocked on the level, do not repeat the same action expecting a different result. Use a wand of opening, slow monster, or another available escape.
- Evidence = Self-teleport calls the player teleport path and clears the swallowed state when teleportation is allowed (`teleport.c`, NetHack 5.0.0).

### Rule 5 — If swallowed, self-zap a wand of opening

- Trigger = The observation exposes swallowed state (`u.uswallow` or an equivalent status flag), or the message stream indicates that the hero has been engulfed. Exact NLE message wording is UNVERIFIED; parse the swallowed state if the wrapper exposes it.
- Action =
  1. Press `z`.
  2. Select the known wand of opening.
  3. At the direction prompt, enter `.` to target yourself.
- Done when = The swallowed flag clears and the hero is no longer inside the monster.
- If it fails = Try Rule 6 if a wand of slow monster is available. If teleportation is allowed, try Rule 7.
- Evidence = `zapyourself()` routes a self-zapped wand of opening to the release-hold routine (`zap.c`, NetHack 5.0.0).

### Rule 6 — If swallowed, use slow monster on the engulfer

- Trigger = The swallowed flag is true and a known wand of slow monster is available.
- Action =
  1. Press `z`.
  2. Select the known wand of slow monster.
  3. Enter a nonzero direction key (for example `h`) at the direction prompt.
  4. Do not enter `.`; that selects the self-zap path rather than the engulfer-target path.
- Done when = The monster is disrupted and the swallowed flag clears.
- If it fails = The monster may have resisted. Do not assume that the first zap succeeded; check the message and swallowed state. Then try Rule 5 if available, or Rule 7 if teleportation is allowed.
- Evidence = The slow-monster effect tests monster resistance, disrupts a whirly engulfer on success, and expels the hero (`zap.c`, NetHack 5.0.0). Energy and fire vortices have MR 30 (`monsters.h`, NetHack 5.0.0).

### Rule 7 — If swallowed, self-teleport rather than teleporting the engulfer on an ordinary level

- Trigger = The swallowed flag is true, a known wand or scroll of teleportation is available, and the level allows teleportation.
- Action =
  - Wand: press `z`, select the wand of teleportation, then enter `.` to self-target.
  - Scroll: press `r`, select the scroll of teleportation.
- Done when = The hero is relocated and the swallowed flag is false.
- If it fails = Check whether the level prevents teleportation. If it does, use a different escape item. Do not substitute a directional zap at the engulfer as the default: on an ordinary teleportable level the hero and engulfer move together.
- Evidence = `tele()` clears the player’s swallowed state; `u_teleport_mon()` has different behavior for no-teleport levels (`teleport.c`, NetHack 5.0.0).

### Rule 8 — Do not use HP thresholds as a general permission to melee

- Trigger = The proposed action is a long-sword melee attack against an energy vortex, fire vortex, or fire elemental.
- Action = Prefer Rule 2 or an escape action. Only consider melee if the bot can establish that the attack will kill the monster in that single blow, or has the relevant resistance and accepts the remaining active-attack and equipment risks. If swallowed and no escape option exists, an attack will hit the engulfer, but the exact terminal command sequence for issuing that attack through this NLE build is UNVERIFIED; do not invent a key sequence.
- Done when = The monster is dead, or the hero is no longer in contact with it.
- If it fails = Re-evaluate HP and swallowed state immediately. Do not repeat melee merely because the prior swing missed: electricity/fire passives can trigger even on a miss if the monster survives.
- Evidence = `uhitm.c` shows the swallowed hit bypass and passive call; `passive()` implements the attack-specific triggers (NetHack 5.0.0).

## Risks and exceptions

1\. The passive is not the same as the engulfing attack. An energy vortex can inflict active shock and drain energy while engulfing, independently of its electric passive. A fire vortex has active fire engulfing as well as passive fire. Fire elementals instead have a direct fire claw attack. Resistance to the passive damage does not necessarily solve all the other attack effects. [5.0 `monsters.h`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/include/monsters.h?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1076-L1100) [5.0 `mhitu.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/mhitu.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1198-L1320)

2\. A missed melee attack can still expose the hero to fire/electric passive damage. The 2-in-3 passive branch is gated by whether the monster remains alive and uncancelled, not by `mhitb`. This is a particularly important distinction for an energy vortex when the hero lacks shock resistance. [5.0 `uhitm.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/uhitm.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L5701-L5803)

3\. HP thresholds are only bounds for one passive roll. At base monster level, surviving a maximum single passive roll requires more than 28 HP against an energy vortex and more than 36 HP against a fire vortex/fire elemental. With the source's 1.5× monster-level cap, those passive-only maxima can become 40 and 52, respectively. Even HP above those figures does not make melee safe: the monster can still engulf or attack, and repeated hero attacks can trigger repeated passives. [5.0 `makemon.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/makemon.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1907-L1936) [5.0 `uhitm.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/uhitm.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L5552-L5803) [5.0 `mhitu.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/mhitu.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1198-L1320)

4\. Shock resistance and fire resistance are not interchangeable. Shock resistance addresses electric damage, not the energy-drain engulf attack. Fire resistance protects against fire HP damage, but a melee hit can still expose the wielded weapon to the fire passive's item effect. [5.0 `mhitu.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/mhitu.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1198-L1320) [5.0 `uhitm.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/uhitm.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L5810-L5874)

5\. Elbereth is environment-dependent. Do not use it as the emergency plan in Gehennom or the Endgame. Also, an already swallowed hero cannot engrave the floor. [5.0 `monmove.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/monmove.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L222-L280) [5.0 `engrave.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/engrave.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L471-L497)

6\. The `v` glyph is ambiguous. It includes vortex species with different active attacks and passive profiles. Some non-passive vortexes are also fast; therefore, the conservative classifier should mark an unidentified `v` as an avoid/escape threat rather than assuming it is harmless. [5.0 `defsym.h`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/include/defsym.h?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1702-L1797) [5.0 `monsters.h`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/include/monsters.h?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1048-L1100)

7\. Do not infer an exact dagger kill count from the species' base level. Monster level and HP can be adjusted, and the HP roll is random. The estimated 14 and 18 hits are averages based on base-level mean HP and a +0 dagger, not hard bounds. [5.0 `makemon.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/makemon.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L967-L1010) [5.0 `weapon.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/weapon.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L197-L282)

8\. Teleporting the engulfer is not normally an escape. On an ordinary teleportable level, teleporting the engulfer takes the swallowed hero along. Self-target the teleport wand, or read the teleport scroll, when the goal is to relocate the hero. [5.0 `teleport.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/teleport.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1589-L1609) [5.0 `teleport.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/teleport.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2124-L2154)
